description: Structured reference data covering every craft/production category named in the ShilpoHub scope document (Handicrafts, Textile Heritage, Folk Art, Musical Heritage, Metal Industry, Clay Industry, Food Heritage, Krishi Shilpo/Agriculture, Fisheries, Cottage Industries). Built for AI training — search, recommendation, chatbots, Heritage DNA Profile, Craft Encyclopedia, Material Traceability, and counterfeit/authenticity checks.
schema_notes: Fields per record: id, name_en, name_bn, category, description, materials[], tools[], technique_steps[], time_required, skill_transmission, regions[], primary_hub, endangerment_level, source_confidence, notes

source_confidence_legend.verified: Cross-checked against UNESCO ICH, Bangladesh GI registry announcements, Banglapedia, Wikipedia, or academic sources during this research session
source_confidence_legend.general_knowledge: Well-established public knowledge, not individually re-verified this session — recommend a field survey / expert or artisan-association review pass before final model training, especially for time estimates and exact village names

coverage_note: This dataset aims for broad coverage of every item named in the source scope document. It is still a starting corpus, not an exhaustive national inventory — Bangladesh has hundreds of hyper-local craft variants (village-specific motifs, sub-castes, seasonal-only crafts) that only direct field documentation can fully capture. Treat entries marked general_knowledge as a first draft to be corrected by artisans/associations, not as final ground truth.

crafts.description: Fine, sheer cotton muslin woven with ornamental motifs directly on the loom using a supplementary discontinuous-weft (brocade) technique. Bangladesh's first GI-registered product and a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage element.
materials: Fine cotton yarn (historically hand-spun; today mostly mill-spun combed cotton, sometimes silk-blended)
tools: Small bamboo needles/spools (tikri) for hand-inserting motif threads
technique_steps: Yarn washing, starching, drying
Warping several hundred to over a thousand threads
Motif planning from memory/paper guide (never printed)
Two weavers typically work together: one throws the main weft, one hand-inserts colored bobbins to build each motif
Trimming, washing, pressing
crafts.time_required: 1–6 months for moderate designs; 6 months–over a year for highly intricate saris, ~8–10 hrs/day, usually two weavers together
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary, family-based; apprenticeship from childhood/teens under a master weaver
regions: Narayanganj — Rupganj, Sonargaon, South Rupshi/Noapara (BSCIC Jamdani Palli), Shitalakshya River belt
crafts.endangerment_level: Vulnerable
crafts.notes: UNESCO ICH (2013); Bangladesh's first GI product (2016).

crafts.category: A. Handicrafts / C. Folk Art / B. Textile Heritage
crafts.description: Hand-embroidered quilt made by running-stitching layers of old cotton saris/dhotis into figurative or geometric motifs — a rural women's upcycling art form.
materials: Cotton thread traditionally drawn from old sari borders
technique_steps: Layer and pin 5–7 old saris
Plan a central motif (often lotus) plus surrounding daily-life scenes
Stitch outward from the center using running stitch and regional variants (Lohori, Lik-Anarasi, Sujni)
Add region-specific border/edge motifs last
Wash and press
crafts.time_required: Weeks to several months per piece, traditionally worked slowly over a season
crafts.skill_transmission: Informal, passed among rural women through shared stitching sessions
crafts.endangerment_level: Moderately at risk in original hand-drawn-thread form
crafts.notes: Jamalpur's Nakshi Kantha is a registered GI product.

crafts.description: Legendary ultra-fine hand-spun cotton ('woven air'), historically world-famous under Mughal patronage, made from the near-extinct Phuti Karpas cotton variety. Now a GI-registered product with active government revival projects.
technique_steps: Cultivate rare Phuti Karpas cotton along riverbanks
Hand-gin and hand-spin into extraordinarily fine yarn (historically spun in humid, river-adjacent conditions)
Hand-weave on narrow looms
Bleach/finish for translucency
crafts.time_required: Months per piece; among the most labor-intensive textiles ever produced
crafts.skill_transmission: Nearly broken chain — largely reconstructed via government/research revival projects rather than unbroken lineage
regions: Historically Dhaka region along the Meghna/Shitalakshya/Brahmaputra rivers; revival cultivation near Kapasia
crafts.endangerment_level: Critically endangered / revival-stage
crafts.notes: 'Dhakai Muslin' is a registered GI product. Recommend expert review before authoritative claims given topic complexity.

crafts.description: Hand-spun, hand-woven cotton cloth associated with self-reliance, coarser and more rustic than Jamdani.
technique_steps: Hand-card raw cotton
Hand-spin on charkha
Warp preparation and sizing
Hand-weave
Wash and sun-dry
crafts.time_required: Several days to a few weeks per piece
crafts.skill_transmission: Family and cooperative/workshop-based
regions: Scattered handloom clusters in Dhaka and Rajshahi divisions
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable but shrinking vs power-loom competition

crafts.description: The broad base handloom-weaving trade producing everyday cotton lungi, gamcha (towel), sari, and yardage cloth, distinct from the specialty Jamdani/Tangail/Rajshahi silk trades — Bangladesh's largest traditional textile employment sector.
technique_steps: Yarn dyeing and sizing
Warping the loom
Plain or twill weaving of body cloth
Cutting and finishing (hemming gamcha/lungi edges)
crafts.time_required: A lungi or gamcha: a few hours; a sari length: 1–2 days
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary weaver families (Tantubay community) and cooperative-run handloom centers
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable but under continuous pressure from powerloom/mill-cloth competition

crafts.description: Full-chain mulberry silk industry — sericulture, reeling, dyeing, weaving — centered on Rajshahi; a registered GI product.
technique_steps: Mulberry cultivation and silkworm rearing
Cocoon boiling and thread reeling
Yarn twisting/throwing
Dyeing
Weaving
Finishing/calendaring
crafts.time_required: Silkworm rearing ~25–30 days; weaving adds days depending on design
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary weaving families plus formal Sericulture Board training
crafts.endangerment_level: Under pressure from imported silk/synthetics

crafts.description: Handwoven cotton and cotton-silk sari with woven (not printed) borders, made by weaver families descended from traditional muslin weavers; recognized as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2025.
tools: Pit loom (some with jacquard attachment for borders)
technique_steps: Yarn dyeing and sizing
Warp setup
Weaving the body (plain/twill)
Weaving woven borders and pallu (extra-warp/extra-weft or jacquard)
Finishing and quality check
crafts.time_required: Roughly 2–5 days per sari; longer for fine jacquard borders
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary, traditionally the Tantubay/Basak weaver community, also cooperative-organized
regions: Tangail district — Karotia, Delduar, Kalihati, Bajitpur, Pathrail upazilas
crafts.endangerment_level: Relatively stable; power-loom copies undercut authentic handloom producers
crafts.notes: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage inscription in 2025.

crafts.description: Handloom tradition of the ethnic Manipuri community producing the Moirang Phee shawl/scarf and phanek (sarong), known for fine geometric temple-border motifs.
technique_steps: Yarn dyeing
Warp setup on backstrap or frame loom
Weaving with continuous attention to the geometric temple-motif border
Hand-finishing edges/fringes
crafts.time_required: A few days to about two weeks depending on border intricacy
crafts.skill_transmission: Passed down within Manipuri households, largely among women weavers
regions: Kamalganj and Kulaura upazilas, Moulvibazar district; Sylhet division
crafts.endangerment_level: Vulnerable — small population base

crafts.description: Handwoven mat from split murta (Schumannianthus dichotomus) cane strips, naturally cooling; comes in normal, jamdani, and nakshi (embroidered) varieties. A registered GI product.
materials: Boiled rice-water, hogplum leaf and boalilota mixture for smoothing/shine
technique_steps: Harvest murta from wetlands
Split into thin even strips
Boil in rice-starch/hogplum-leaf mixture
Sun-dry
Weave by hand (plain, jamdani-style brocade, or fully embroidered nakshi)
Trim and finish edges
crafts.time_required: ~5 days for a normal mat, 8–9 days for jamdani-style, up to a month for nakshi (embroidered)
crafts.skill_transmission: Family-based; historically strongest in the Manipuri community of Sylhet
crafts.endangerment_level: Vulnerable — livelihood of ~8,000 weavers
crafts.notes: National ICH listing (2007); registered GI product.

crafts.description: Wheel-thrown and hand-built clay vessels made by hereditary Kumar/Pal potter communities using local clay. Netrokona's Bijoypur white clay (a registered GI product) is a key raw-material source for fine pottery/ceramics.
materials: Bijoypur white clay (Netrokona) for finer wares
technique_steps: Clay collection and purification
Wedging to remove air
Throwing on wheel or hand-building larger vessels
Sun-drying 1–3 days
Decorating (incising, slip painting, combing)
Kiln firing ~6–12 hours
Cooling and sorting
crafts.time_required: Hours to shape, 1–3 days to dry, plus a shared firing cycle of 6–12 hours
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary within Kumar/Pal potter communities
crafts.endangerment_level: Moderate risk from plastic/metal vessel competition
crafts.notes: Netrokona's Bijoypur white clay is a registered GI product.

crafts.description: Fired unglazed clay used for architectural relief panels (e.g. Kantanagar Temple, Puthia temple complex) and standalone art plaques/sculptures.
technique_steps: Refine clay to workable consistency
Mold or hand-sculpt
Carve fine detail while leather-hard
Slow air-drying
Kiln-fire at high temperature
Assemble/mount panels onto architecture
crafts.time_required: Days per panel (with drying); large architectural commissions historically took months to years
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary artisan workshops; also art-school-trained sculptors today
crafts.endangerment_level: Traditional architectural-scale skill is rare

crafts.description: Hand-molded, painted clay figurines/toys sold at village fairs (Poush Mela, Baishakhi Mela).
tools: Small kiln or open firing pit
technique_steps: Shape clay by hand or mold
Air-dry
Low-temperature firing
Hand-paint folk motifs
Apply varnish
crafts.time_required: A few hours to a day per piece
crafts.skill_transmission: Family-based, often a secondary trade of pottery families
crafts.endangerment_level: Declining vs plastic toys

crafts.description: Metal-casting and hammering craft producing bell-metal (kansha) and brass (peetal) utensils, idols, and decorative items, historically centered in Dhamrai.
tools: Sand molds or lost-wax clay molds
technique_steps: Melt alloy in furnace
Cast in sand molds or lost-wax method for detailed idols
Hammer flat sheets/blanks into shape over an anvil for utensils
Anneal periodically while hammering
Engrave/emboss decoration
Polish and finish
crafts.time_required: Simple utensils: 1–2 days; detailed cast idols: 1–4 weeks
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary Kansari (bell-metal worker) and Karmakar (metalworker) families
crafts.endangerment_level: Endangered — rising metal costs, competition from stainless steel

crafts.description: Hand-hammered copper vessels, ceremonial items, and decorative products, often made alongside brass/bell-metal in the same workshops.
technique_steps: Melt and cast copper into blanks or use sheet copper directly
Hammer/raise into vessel shapes
Anneal periodically
Engrave decorative patterns
Polish
crafts.time_required: 1–3 days per item depending on size/detail
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary metalworker (Karmakar) families
crafts.endangerment_level: Endangered, small artisan base

crafts.description: Blacksmith craft (Karmakar/Kamar community) forging knives (dao, boti), sickles (kaste), plow blades, and other hand tools essential to farming and household life.
materials: Iron/steel stock (often recycled leaf-spring or scrap steel)
technique_steps: Heat raw steel stock in the forge until malleable
Hammer-forge into the tool's rough shape on the anvil
Reheat and refine the edge geometry
Quench to harden the blade
Temper by controlled reheating to reduce brittleness
Grind and sharpen the edge
Fit a wood/bamboo handle
crafts.time_required: A single tool (knife/sickle): a few hours; larger plow blades: up to a day
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary within blacksmith (Kamar) caste communities, workshop-based (often roadside forges)
regions: Notable concentrations in Bogura, Rajshahi, and Sirajganj rural markets
crafts.primary_hub: Rural blacksmith markets nationwide (no single dominant hub)
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable as a rural livelihood, though factory-made tools are increasing competition

crafts.description: Baskets, fish traps, furniture, mats, and structural items woven or built from split bamboo.
technique_steps: Select and cut mature bamboo
Split into strips of required width
Sun-dry or smoke-treat against insects
Weave into baskets/mats/panels or assemble into furniture frames
Trim, sand, finish
crafts.time_required: Simple baskets: a few hours; furniture: several days
crafts.skill_transmission: Widely practiced village skill, hereditary among Rakhain and other bamboo-craft communities
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable as livelihood; fine artisanal work losing ground to plastic

crafts.description: Furniture (chairs, baskets, trays) woven from flexible cane/rattan, often combined with bamboo framing.
technique_steps: Harvest and split raw cane
Soak/steam for flexibility
Weave around frames or freestanding
Bend and shape while pliable, then dry to set
Sand and varnish
crafts.time_required: Small items: a day or less; furniture: several days to two weeks
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary within cane-craft families, workshop apprenticeship
crafts.endangerment_level: Moderate — furniture demand keeps it relatively stable

crafts.description: Handmade bags, rugs, wall hangings, and decorative items woven or macraméd from jute fiber — Bangladesh's iconic 'golden fiber.'
technique_steps: Retting and stripping raw jute (usually done before reaching artisans)
Spin fiber into twine
Dye if colored items desired
Weave on handloom or hand-knot/macramé
Finish edges, add linings/hardware
crafts.time_required: Bags: hours to a day; woven rugs: several days
crafts.skill_transmission: Village weaving skill plus NGO/design-led craft cooperatives
crafts.endangerment_level: Growing sector — eco-friendly material demand

crafts.description: Carving of conch shell (shankha) bangles (shakha) — traditionally worn by married Bengali Hindu women — and decorative shell items, historically centered in Dhaka's Shakhari Bazar.
materials: Conch shells (imported, mainly Sri Lanka/South India)
technique_steps: Select and clean raw shells
Cut ring-shaped bangle blanks by saw
File to shape and smooth edges
Carve decorative patterns on select pieces
Polish
Pair for sale
crafts.time_required: Plain bangles: a few hours; carved pieces: a day or more
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary within the Shakhari artisan caste community
crafts.endangerment_level: Endangered — shrinking community, rising import costs

crafts.description: Bowls, buttons, jewelry, and ornaments carved from cleaned, polished coconut shells.
technique_steps: Clean and dry shells
Cut to shape
Carve/engrave decoration
Sand smooth
Polish and varnish
crafts.time_required: A few hours per small item
crafts.skill_transmission: Village-level craft, supplementary livelihood in coconut-growing areas
crafts.endangerment_level: Small, stable niche craft

crafts.description: Hand-tooled and stitched leather goods — bags, shoes, belts, decorative items.
technique_steps: Cut tanned leather to pattern
Dye/finish surface
Hand-tool or emboss motifs
Hand- or machine-stitch pieces
Attach hardware, finish edges
crafts.time_required: Belts/wallets: hours; bags/footwear: a day to a few days
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary artisan families and vocational-trained workers
crafts.endangerment_level: Growing export sector; traditional hand-tooling is a shrinking niche

crafts.description: Hand-carved furniture, decorative panels, and household items, notably elaborately carved Sylheti and Chittagong-style furniture.
materials: Local hardwoods (mahogany, teak/segun, mango, jackfruit wood)
technique_steps: Season and dry timber
Cut and shape components
Hand-carve relief decoration
Join components
Sand
Polish/varnish
crafts.time_required: Small items: a day; hand-carved furniture: 1–4 weeks
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary carpenter (Sutradhar) families, plus workshop apprenticeship
crafts.endangerment_level: Traditional hand-carving declining vs machine-cut furniture

crafts.description: Handwoven or hand-stitched fans made from palm leaf, bamboo, cloth, or cane, often decorated with colorful embroidery or painted motifs.
materials: Palm leaf (tal pata) or bamboo strips
technique_steps: Cut and dry palm leaf or split bamboo into strips
Shape into a fan form (round, heart-shaped, or hand-shaped)
Weave or stitch the fan body
Attach a handle
Edge with colored cloth/thread and add decorative embroidery or painted motifs
crafts.time_required: A few hours per fan
crafts.skill_transmission: Village household craft, often practiced by women as a home-based livelihood
crafts.endangerment_level: Declining household-utility demand due to electric fans, but a growing decorative/tourist-souvenir niche

crafts.description: Traditional hand-fabricated jewelry including silver filigree work, beadwork, and folk-motif ornaments distinct from mainstream urban goldsmithing.
tools: Small furnace/torch for melting and soldering metal
technique_steps: Melt and draw silver into fine wire (for filigree)
Shape and solder wire into lace-like filigree patterns, or set/string beads
Engrave or emboss surface detail
Polish the finished piece
crafts.time_required: Simple beadwork: hours; fine filigree silver pieces: several days
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary within traditional goldsmith/silversmith (Swarnakar) artisan families, and among Hill Tracts indigenous jewelry-making communities
regions: Chattogram Hill Tracts (indigenous beadwork/silver traditions among Chakma, Marma, and other communities)
crafts.endangerment_level: Vulnerable — competition from machine-made jewelry

crafts.description: Vibrant hand-painted decorative art on cycle-rickshaw bodies, hoods, and back panels — a distinctly urban Bangladeshi folk-art form.
technique_steps: Prime the metal panel
Sketch freehand from memory
Paint base colors/shapes
Add fine detail, outlines, shading
Attach decorative trim
Varnish
crafts.time_required: Full panel set for one rickshaw: roughly 2–5 days
crafts.skill_transmission: Workshop apprenticeship under a master painter (ustad), concentrated in Old Dhaka
crafts.endangerment_level: Endangered — declining rickshaw numbers, rise of printed vinyl decals
crafts.notes: UNESCO inscribed 'Rickshaws and rickshaw painting in Dhaka City' as Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2023 — recommend verifying exact wording before final publication.

crafts.description: Ephemeral decorative floor/wall painting made with rice-paste, drawn for festivals (Pohela Boishakh, weddings, religious occasions).
materials: Colored powders/natural dyes for multi-color alpana
technique_steps: Mix rice flour into a smooth paste
Dip fingers/applicator
Freehand-draw motifs directly on a swept floor/wall from memory
Complete large communal designs collaboratively for festivals
crafts.time_required: Minutes for small motifs; hours for large communal festival alpana
crafts.skill_transmission: Informally passed among women in households/communities
regions: Practiced nationwide, especially prominent in Dhaka's Pohela Boishakh celebrations
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable living seasonal tradition (not typically sold as a product)

crafts.description: Narrative scroll paintings unrolled panel-by-panel while the artist (Patua) sings an accompanying narrative song.
materials: Natural pigments or modern poster/tempera colors
technique_steps: Paste paper onto cloth backing
Sketch sequential narrative panels
Apply pigments panel by panel
Outline and detail
Join panels into a scroll
Compose an accompanying oral narrative song
crafts.time_required: Several days to a few weeks per full scroll
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary within Patua artist families, who are also the performers
regions: Living tradition much stronger in West Bengal, India (Naya village, Midnapore); scattered revivalist practice in greater Mymensingh and Dhaka's art community
crafts.primary_hub: Scattered / weak domestic hub in Bangladesh
crafts.endangerment_level: Endangered in Bangladesh specifically
crafts.notes: Needs the most field verification of all entries — confirm currently active Bangladeshi Patua families before treating as a strong domestic category.

crafts.description: Hand-crafted decorative and ritual/festival masks, historically associated with folk performance, Gambhira dance-drama of Rajshahi/Chapainawabganj, and indigenous community festivals in the Chattogram Hill Tracts.
tools: Clay-modeling tools (to make the base mold)
technique_steps: Sculpt a clay mold of the desired face/figure
Layer wet papier-mâché over the mold and let dry, or carve directly from wood
Remove the dried papier-mâché shell from the mold
Sand and smooth the surface
Paint with bold, expressive colors and folk motifs
Varnish for durability
crafts.time_required: A single mask: 2–5 days including drying time
crafts.skill_transmission: Passed within folk-performance troupe families and craft workshops
crafts.endangerment_level: Vulnerable — tied to the shrinking practice of traditional mask-dance performances

crafts.description: Broad category of traditional two-dimensional folk painting on paper, cloth, or wood panels, covering styles beyond scroll painting — including devotional imagery, decorative panel art, and painted items for household/ritual use.
materials: Handmade paper, cloth, or wood panel
technique_steps: Prepare the painting surface (prime cloth/wood or select paper)
Sketch the composition
Apply base colors and build up layers
Add fine linework and detailing
Seal/varnish if on wood or cloth
crafts.time_required: Hours to several days depending on size and detail
crafts.skill_transmission: Family workshops and, increasingly, formal fine-arts training
regions: Practiced in scattered artisan pockets nationwide, with concentration in Dhaka's craft and art communities
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable as a broad, evolving category rather than a single endangered craft
crafts.notes: This is a broad umbrella category — recommend narrowing to specific regional sub-styles once field data is available, to avoid overlap with Patachitra and Rickshaw Art.

crafts.description: Hand-lettering art tradition covering both Arabic/Islamic calligraphy (common on mosque interiors, religious art, and decorative pieces) and artistic Bengali script lettering used in folk and contemporary design.
materials: Handmade or fine paper, canvas, or wood panel
tools: Qalam (reed pen) or specialized calligraphy brush
technique_steps: Prepare ink and cut/shape the qalam nib
Rule faint guide lines for proportion
Practice and then execute the script in a chosen style (e.g., Naskh, Thuluth for Arabic; decorative styles for Bengali)
Apply gold leaf or color accents if desired
Mount or frame the finished piece
crafts.time_required: Hours for a single composition; more for elaborate framed/gilded pieces
crafts.skill_transmission: Formal apprenticeship under a calligraphy master (ustad), often linked to madrasa or art-school training
regions: Practiced nationwide in mosque decoration and art communities
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable niche craft, sustained by religious/decorative demand

crafts.description: Handcrafting of the dotara, a four-stringed folk lute central to Baul and Bhawaiya music.
tools: Lathe or hand tools for hollowing
technique_steps: Select and season a wood block for the body
Hollow the body by hand
Shape the neck/headstock
Attach the soundboard
Fit pegs and string
Tune, test, and finish/polish
crafts.time_required: Roughly 1–3 weeks per instrument
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary instrument-maker families, often linked to Baul musician communities
crafts.endangerment_level: Vulnerable — small, aging artisan base

crafts.description: Handcrafting of the ektara, a one-stringed drone instrument, most famously used by Baul singers.
technique_steps: Select and dry a hard-shelled gourd
Hollow it to form a resonating chamber
Stretch/fix a skin membrane over the opening
Fit a bamboo neck
String from neck tip to membrane center
Tune and finish
crafts.time_required: Roughly 1–3 days per instrument
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary/community-based, tied to Baul musician communities
crafts.endangerment_level: Vulnerable

crafts.description: Handcrafting of the tabla, a paired hand-drum used in classical, devotional, and folk music, involving wood-turning for the shells and multi-layer skin membrane preparation.
materials: Seasoned wood (for the dayan/treble drum shell) or metal/clay (for the bayan/bass drum shell)
A paste of iron filings, rice starch, and gum (syahi) applied to the drumhead center
tools: Wood lathe for turning the shell
technique_steps: Turn/shape the wooden or metal shell
Prepare goat skin membranes in layered rings
Stretch and lace the skin over the shell with leather braiding
Apply and burnish the syahi (tuning paste) in a precise circular pattern on the drumhead
Fit wooden tuning blocks under the lacing
Tune by adjusting lacing tension and block position
crafts.time_required: Roughly 1–2 weeks per pair including skin-drying and syahi-application time
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary within specialized instrument-maker families, concentrated among a small number of workshops
regions: Historically linked to classical-music patron communities in Dhaka and Chattogram
crafts.endangerment_level: Endangered — very few remaining specialist makers

crafts.description: Handcrafting of the dhol, a large barrel-shaped folk drum central to wedding processions, festivals, and folk performances.
materials: Wood (for the barrel shell, often mango or jackfruit wood staves)
Animal skin (cow or goat) for both drumheads
Metal rings (to hold the skin taut)
technique_steps: Shape the wooden barrel shell (stave-built or hollowed from a single log)
Prepare and stretch animal skin over metal rings for each drumhead
Fit the skin heads onto both ends of the shell
Lace rope in a zigzag pattern between the two heads to hold them in place and allow tension adjustment
Tune by tightening the lacing
crafts.time_required: Roughly 3–7 days per drum
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary within drum-maker (often linked to leatherworking) artisan families
regions: Village drum-maker clusters nationwide, notable presence in greater Dhaka and Chattogram
crafts.primary_hub: No single dominant hub — nationwide rural workshops
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable — strong ongoing demand tied to weddings and festivals

crafts.description: Handcrafting of the bamboo transverse flute (bashi), a central instrument in Bengali folk and devotional music.
materials: Seasoned bamboo of specific diameter/wall thickness
tools: Hot metal rod or drill for burning/boring finger holes
technique_steps: Select and season bamboo of the right diameter
Cut to the desired length
Mark finger-hole positions based on the target musical scale
Burn or drill the holes
Fine-tune each hole's size/position by ear against a reference pitch
Smooth and finish the exterior
crafts.time_required: A few hours to a day per flute, including tuning
crafts.skill_transmission: Often a skill combining craft and musicianship — many makers are also players; passed informally or through folk-music communities
regions: Scattered artisan-musicians nationwide, notably in rural Kushtia, Rajshahi, and riverine districts
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable niche, sustained by continued folk-music performance demand

crafts.description: Assembly and repair craft for the hand-pumped reed harmonium widely used in devotional, folk, and light-classical Bengali music — a more mechanically complex, workshop-based instrument craft than most other Musical Heritage entries.
tools: Tuning reference (tuning fork or reference pitch)
technique_steps: Build or source the wooden casing
Install and align the metal reed set
Assemble the bellows mechanism
Fit keys and internal valve/stop mechanisms
Tune each reed individually by filing
Test and adjust bellows air-tightness
crafts.time_required: Full assembly/build: 1–3 weeks; tuning-only repair work: a few hours to a day
crafts.skill_transmission: Workshop-based apprenticeship, more industrial/mechanical in nature than most other listed crafts
regions: Dhaka (main center for harmonium workshops and repair)
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable niche — steady demand from religious and music institutions

crafts.name_en: Traditional Sweets (Mishti) — Chomchom, Rasmalai, Kachagolla, Rasgolla, Monda, Khaza
crafts.description: Bengal's dairy-and-sugar confectionery tradition — a cluster of regionally distinct, GI-recognized sweets made by hereditary confectioner (Moira/Ghosh) families, each tied to a specific town's water, milk, or technique.
materials: Chhena (fresh curdled milk cheese) or khoa (reduced milk solids)
Coconut or mawa flakes (for garnish, e.g. chomchom)
technique_steps: Boil fresh milk and curdle it with an acid (lemon/vinegar/whey) to form chhena, or reduce milk slowly to khoa
Strain and knead the chhena to a smooth dough
Shape into the sweet's characteristic form (oval for Porabari chomchom, flat rounds for kachagolla, etc.)
Boil shaped pieces in sugar syrup until cooked through
Garnish (coconut/mawa flakes) or soak in flavored cream (for rasmalai)
Cool and pack, often in earthen pots for regional specialties
crafts.time_required: Several hours per batch, including milk-reduction and syrup-boiling time
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary within confectioner (Moira/Ghosh) family workshops (karkhana)
regions: Kushtia (Tiler Khaza, sesame sweet — GI product)
crafts.primary_hub: Multiple GI-protected town-specific hubs (Tangail, Comilla, Natore, Gopalganj, Mymensingh, Kushtia)
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable and commercially strong — most entries here are actively GI-protected and thriving
crafts.notes: All six named sweets are officially registered GI products of Bangladesh (Department of Patents, Designs and Trademarks).

crafts.description: Bangladesh's most famous traditional sweet yogurt (mishti doi), a registered GI product, credited to confectioner Ghetu Ghosh of Sherpur, Bogura, and attributed to local milk and water quality.
materials: Full-cream cow's milk (deshi dudh, notably from Sahiwal-breed cows)
A starter/seed portion of previously set yogurt
tools: Large kadhai (wok) set over an open coal or gas fire
Traditional clay ovens for holding/setting the pots
technique_steps: Boil large quantities of full-cream milk in a kadhai over several hours, reducing its volume
Continuously stir and periodically pour boiling milk from a height back into the kadhai to prevent fat separation
Mix sugar into the reduced milk
Fill unglazed earthen pots to the brim with the sweetened reduced milk
Add a starter/seed portion of prior yogurt to each pot
Set the pots around ovens to ferment and firm up
crafts.time_required: Several hours of milk-reduction plus an overnight (or longer) fermentation/setting period
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary within the Ghosh confectioner community of Sherpur, now also practiced by other local families; the wider trade also involves Pal-community potters who supply the earthen pots
regions: Sherpur Upazila, Bogura district (~24 km from Bogura town, along the Jamuna River)
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable and thriving — GI certification (2023) drove a 40%+ increase in annual turnover, now exceeding Tk 14 billion/year

crafts.description: Hand-shaped and hand-decorated rice-flour cake (pitha), carved or pressed with intricate floral/geometric surface patterns before frying — a winter-festival specialty, traditionally made during Poush/Nabanna harvest celebrations.
tools: Small carving knife or comb-like tool for pressing surface patterns
technique_steps: Prepare a smooth rice-flour dough
Roll and shape into flat pieces
Hand-carve or press decorative motifs into the surface using a small knife or comb tool
Deep-fry until golden
Dip or coat in sugar/molasses syrup
crafts.time_required: A batch: a few hours, including dough preparation, carving, and frying
crafts.skill_transmission: Informal household skill, passed among women, strongest during the winter Poush-Parbon festival season
regions: Practiced nationwide, especially in rural Bengal during winter festivals — notable in Rangpur, Comilla, and Faridpur
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable seasonal tradition

crafts.category: G. Food Heritage / H. Krishi Shilpo
crafts.description: Cultivation and preparation of shatkora, a bitter citrus fruit iconic to Sylhet cuisine, used fresh, pickled, or dried in signature regional curries.
technique_steps: Harvest ripe shatkora
Slice and remove excess bitterness by parboiling or salting (depending on preparation)
Use fresh in curries, or sun-dry slices for later use, or pickle with oil/spices for long-term storage
crafts.time_required: Fresh use: same day; pickled/dried preparation: several days of processing and drying/curing
crafts.skill_transmission: Household/village-level agricultural and culinary knowledge, specific to Sylhet regional cuisine
regions: Sylhet division, especially Sylhet and Moulvibazar districts
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable — strongly tied to living regional cuisine, growing national popularity

crafts.description: Honey harvesting from both wild forest hives (notably the Sundarbans mangrove forest, gathered by traditional mouals/honey collectors) and managed apiary beekeeping, especially tied to the Sundarbans and mustard-flower (sarisha) blooming season.
materials: Smoke (for calming bees during wild harvesting)
tools: Smoker (bundle of smoldering leaves/wood for wild collection)
Protective cloth wrapping (traditional, minimal protective gear)
Modern movable-frame hive boxes (for apiary beekeeping)
technique_steps: Wild collection (Sundarbans): mouals travel by boat into the mangrove forest during the permitted honey season, locate wild hives, use smoke to calm bees, and manually cut honeycomb from tree branches
Apiary beekeeping: place managed hive boxes near mustard/litchi/sesame fields during flowering season
Extract honey by pressing/straining comb or using a centrifugal extractor
Filter and bottle the honey
crafts.time_required: Wild Sundarbans harvesting season runs roughly April–June; apiary harvesting cycles every few weeks during a flowering season
crafts.skill_transmission: Wild collection: hereditary moual (honey-hunter) community knowledge, passed father to son; apiary beekeeping increasingly taught through government/NGO training programs
regions: Sundarbans (Khulna, Satkhira, Bagerhat) for wild forest honey
Rajshahi, Chapainawabganj, Natore, and Meherpur for mustard-flower apiary honey
crafts.endangerment_level: Wild honey collection is a high-risk, physically dangerous traditional livelihood (tiger-attack risk) with a shrinking moual community; apiary beekeeping is a growing sector

crafts.description: Cultivation of heritage and aromatic rice varieties preserved by farming communities, several of which are now GI-registered — grown using traditional, often organic, low-input methods distinct from high-yield modern varieties.
materials: Heirloom/aromatic paddy seed stock preserved and re-sown by farmers season to season
tools: Traditional threshing and husking equipment (dheki, a foot-pounded husking device)
technique_steps: Select and preserve seed stock from the previous season's best plants
Prepare and transplant seedlings into flooded paddy fields
Manage growth through the Aman (monsoon) or Boro (dry) season depending on variety
Harvest by hand with a sickle
Thresh and traditionally husk using a dheki (foot-operated wooden pounder)
Sun-dry and store
crafts.time_required: A full growing season (roughly 4–5 months for most Aman varieties)
crafts.skill_transmission: Generational farming knowledge, seed-saving traditions passed within farming families and local seed networks
regions: Nationwide (Bangladesh Kalijira black cumin rice — GI product)
crafts.endangerment_level: Vulnerable — high-yield modern varieties have displaced much indigenous rice cultivation, though GI recognition is reviving some varieties
crafts.notes: Kataribhog (Dinajpur), Tulshimala (Sherpur), and Kalijira are all registered GI products.

crafts.description: Cultivation of named heritage mango varieties from Bangladesh's northwestern mango belt, several of which are GI-registered, grown in century-old orchards using traditional grafting and orchard-management knowledge.
materials: Grafted mango saplings of named heritage varieties
technique_steps: Propagate trees via grafting to preserve the exact heritage variety's characteristics
Manage the orchard through flowering and fruit-set season
Hand-harvest at the correct ripeness stage using a pole and basket to avoid bruising
Sort and grade by size/ripeness for market
crafts.time_required: A full annual growing cycle from flowering (Feb–Mar) to harvest (May–Jul depending on variety)
crafts.skill_transmission: Generational orchard-keeping knowledge in the Chapainawabganj/Rajshahi mango belt
regions: Chapainawabganj (Khirsapat/Himsagar, Langra, Ashwina mango — all GI products)
Rajshahi & Chapainawabganj jointly (Fazli mango — GI product)
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable and commercially strong, actively GI-protected
crafts.notes: Khirsapat, Langra, Ashwina, Fazli, and Haribhanga are all registered GI mango varieties.

crafts.description: Cultivation of jackfruit (Bangladesh's national fruit) and traditional home-based processing into seeds, chips, and preserved products.
materials: Jackfruit tree cultivation (often backyard/homestead trees rather than orchard monoculture)
Mustard oil coating (traditionally used on hands/tools to manage the fruit's sticky latex)
tools: Knife (with oil coating to prevent sticking)
technique_steps: Harvest ripe jackfruit from homestead or orchard trees
Extract the fleshy bulbs by hand (oil-coated hands/tools to manage latex)
Eat fresh, or dry/process the flesh and seeds
Seeds are often dried and later boiled or roasted as a separate food item
crafts.time_required: Harvesting and processing a single fruit: an hour or two
crafts.skill_transmission: Widespread household/homestead knowledge nationwide
regions: Gazipur, Tangail, and greater Dhaka division are notably productive belts
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable — jackfruit is the national fruit with strong ongoing cultivation

crafts.description: Tea leaf cultivation and processing across Bangladesh's historic tea-garden belt, involving hand-plucking and, in smaller traditional operations, hand-rolling and pan-firing of leaves alongside industrial factory processing.
technique_steps: Hand-pluck the top two leaves and a bud from tea bushes
Wither the plucked leaves by spreading them out to reduce moisture
Roll the leaves (by hand in small traditional operations, or by machine in factories) to release enzymes and shape the leaf
Allow controlled oxidation/fermentation
Fire/dry the leaves to halt oxidation and stabilize the tea
Sort and grade the finished tea
crafts.time_required: A single day's cycle from plucking to finished dried tea in most processing operations
crafts.skill_transmission: A mix of hereditary tea-garden worker communities (many descended from historic indentured-labor migrant communities) and formal estate-management training
regions: Sylhet division — Sreemangal, Moulvibazar, Habiganj (Bangladesh's principal tea belt)
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable, large-scale commercial sector; the traditional hand-processing side is a smaller niche within it

crafts.description: Cultivation and traditional processing (sun-drying, grinding) of regional spices and medicinal herbs — including turmeric, ginger, black cumin (kalijira), betel leaf, and various homestead herbal remedies.
materials: Spice/herb crop seed or rootstock (turmeric rhizome, ginger rhizome, betel vine cuttings, etc.)
tools: Traditional grinding stone (shil-nora) or mortar and pestle
technique_steps: Plant and cultivate the crop through its growing season
Harvest at the correct maturity (e.g., rhizomes dug up, leaves hand-picked)
Sun-dry raw material where applicable (turmeric, ginger)
Hand-grind or pound into powder using a traditional grinding stone
Package/store for household use or sale
crafts.time_required: Growing season varies by crop (a few months for turmeric/ginger); drying and grinding adds several days of post-harvest processing
crafts.skill_transmission: Widespread generational farming and household herbal-medicine knowledge
regions: Rajshahi sweet betel leaf belt (a registered GI product)
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable — steady domestic demand
crafts.notes: Rajshahi sweet betel leaf (pan) is a registered GI product.

crafts.description: Farmer-led practice of selecting, drying, and storing seed stock of heirloom crop varieties season to season, preserving genetic diversity outside formal seed-company supply chains.
materials: Selected seed heads/grains/rhizomes from the healthiest plants of a heritage variety
Ash, neem leaves, or other traditional natural preservatives to deter pests in storage
tools: Traditional storage containers (clay pots, bamboo baskets, jute sacks)
technique_steps: Select seed stock from the best-performing plants at harvest
Thoroughly sun-dry to reduce moisture and prevent rot
Mix with traditional natural pest-deterrents if needed
Store in clay pots, bamboo containers, or sacks in a dry location
Re-sow the following season, repeating selection each cycle
crafts.time_required: Ongoing seasonal cycle rather than a single discrete task
crafts.skill_transmission: Generational farming-family knowledge; increasingly supported by community seed banks and NGO-led conservation programs
regions: Farming communities nationwide, with notable community seed-bank initiatives in northern districts (Dinajpur, Rangpur)
crafts.endangerment_level: Vulnerable — commercial hybrid seed adoption is steadily eroding indigenous seed-saving practice

crafts.description: Traditional sun-drying and salting of fish for long-term preservation, a major coastal/riverine livelihood and food-heritage product, especially from the Chattogram coast and Sundarbans-adjacent areas.
technique_steps: Clean and gut freshly caught fish
Salt the fish if making a salted-dry variety (some varieties are dried unsalted)
Lay fish out on raised bamboo racks in direct sun and wind
Turn periodically over several days to ensure even drying and prevent spoilage/insect damage
Once fully dried, sort, pack, and store or transport to market
crafts.time_required: Roughly 3–10 days of sun-drying depending on fish size, weather, and humidity
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary within fishing communities, often a household/family-run seasonal operation
regions: Cox's Bazar (Nazirartek — Bangladesh's largest dry-fish processing site)
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable, large-scale coastal livelihood industry

crafts.description: Hand-knotted fishing nets of various traditional designs (cast nets, gill nets, fixed traps) made and repaired by riverine and coastal fishing communities.
materials: Weights (lead or clay) for cast nets
Floats (traditionally wood or dried gourd/shola pith)
tools: Mesh gauge (a flat stick used to keep knot spacing uniform)
technique_steps: Wind twine onto a netting needle
Knot mesh in consistent rows using a mesh gauge to keep spacing uniform
Shape the net to the required pattern (rectangular gill net, conical cast net, etc.)
Attach weights along the bottom edge and floats along the top edge as needed
Repair worn sections of existing nets by re-knotting damaged mesh
crafts.time_required: A full cast net: several days; ongoing repair work is a continuous daily task in fishing villages
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary within fishing communities, learned informally from childhood
regions: Riverine and coastal fishing villages nationwide — notable in Barishal, Bhola, Chandpur (Padma-Meghna belt) and Cox's Bazar/Chattogram coast
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable as a livelihood skill, though factory-made nets are increasingly common

crafts.description: Hand construction of traditional wooden river and coastal boats (many regionally distinct designs — e.g., the racing/ceremonial 'Sampan' and 'Kosha nouka', cargo 'Panshi', and fishing 'Balam' boats), built without formal blueprints using inherited proportional knowledge.
materials: Timber (traditionally jarul, chambal, or sal wood; increasingly mixed with more available timbers)
Coir/jute caulking fiber for sealing seams
tools: Adze and hand axe for shaping timber
Caulking tools for sealing hull seams
Measuring cord (used instead of formal blueprints, based on inherited proportional ratios)
technique_steps: Select and season timber
Shape the keel and hull planks by hand using an adze/axe
Assemble the hull plank by plank (often edge-joined or lapped, depending on regional style) using wooden pegs and/or iron fasteners
Caulk seams with coir/jute fiber to make the hull watertight
Apply a coal-tar/bitumen waterproof coating
Fit oars, sails, or (for modern boats) an engine mount
Launch and test
crafts.time_required: A small fishing boat: 1–3 weeks; larger cargo or ceremonial racing boats: several weeks to a few months
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary within traditional boat-builder (Mistri) communities, working from memorized proportional knowledge rather than formal drawings
crafts.endangerment_level: Vulnerable — competition from engine-boat/fiberglass construction and shrinking demand for traditional wooden hull designs

crafts.description: Small-batch, cold- or hot-process soap made in home-based or cottage workshops, often using natural oils and traditional botanical ingredients.
materials: Vegetable oils (coconut, mustard, or palm oil)
Natural additives (herbs, essential oils, turmeric, neem)
technique_steps: Measure and combine oils with a lye solution (saponification)
Mix/blend until the mixture reaches 'trace' (thickened) consistency
Add natural additives, herbs, or fragrance
Pour into molds
Cure for several weeks to allow full saponification and hardening
Cut into bars and package
crafts.time_required: Mixing/pouring: a few hours; curing: typically 4–6 weeks before the soap is ready to use
crafts.skill_transmission: Small-scale cottage entrepreneurship, often women-led home businesses, increasingly taught through NGO/vocational training programs
regions: Home-based cottage producers nationwide, concentrated around Dhaka and district-town small-business clusters
crafts.primary_hub: Nationwide cottage/home-business network (no single traditional hub)
crafts.endangerment_level: Growing modern cottage-industry sector rather than an endangered heritage craft

crafts.description: Small-batch candle-making, historically important for lighting and religious/festival use, now largely a decorative and gift-item cottage industry.
materials: Dyes and fragrance oils (for decorative candles)
technique_steps: Melt wax to the correct temperature
Add dye/fragrance if desired
Set a wick in a mold or use repeated dipping for traditional dipped candles
Pour or dip to build up the candle
Cool, unmold, and trim the wick
crafts.time_required: A few hours per batch
crafts.skill_transmission: Cottage-industry skill, often taught through small-business/vocational training programs
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable modern cottage-industry niche

crafts.description: Home-based production of herbal skincare and haircare items (ubtan/face packs, herbal hair oils, natural scrubs) using traditional Bengali botanical beauty recipes.
materials: Herbs and botanicals (turmeric, neem, sandalwood, multani mati/clay, henna)
tools: Traditional grinding stone (shil-nora) or modern grinder
technique_steps: Dry and grind raw herbs/botanicals into fine powder
Blend powders with oils or other binders according to a traditional recipe
Package into jars/sachets
For liquid products (hair oils), infuse herbs into base oil through gentle heating and straining
crafts.time_required: A batch: a few hours to a day, including drying/infusing time for some recipes
crafts.skill_transmission: Household/family beauty-recipe knowledge, increasingly commercialized through small women-led cottage businesses
crafts.endangerment_level: Growing modern cottage-industry sector

crafts.description: Cold-pressed extraction of mustard, sesame, or coconut oil using the traditional bullock- or motor-driven ghani (wooden oil press), valued for retaining more flavor/nutrients than modern refined-oil processing.
materials: Mustard seed, sesame seed, or dried coconut
tools: Ghani (traditional wooden/stone oil press, historically bullock-driven, now often motorized)
technique_steps: Clean and dry the oilseed
Load seed into the ghani's crushing chamber
Slowly rotate the press (traditionally via a bullock walking in a circle; today often a small motor) to crush and press oil from the seed over several hours
Strain the extracted oil to remove seed residue (khoil/oil-cake, itself sold as animal feed or fertilizer)
Bottle and store the oil
crafts.time_required: Several hours per pressing batch
crafts.skill_transmission: Hereditary within traditional oil-presser (Kalu/Teli) community workshops
regions: Rural market towns nationwide, notable traditional ghani presses in Faridpur, Kushtia, and greater Rajshahi
crafts.primary_hub: No single dominant hub — rural market-town ghani presses nationwide
crafts.endangerment_level: Vulnerable — competition from industrial refined-oil production, though a growing 'cold-pressed/pure oil' consumer niche is reviving some ghani operations

crafts.name_en: Village Food Processing (Chira, Muri, Gur, Pickles)
crafts.category: J. Cottage Industries / H. Krishi Shilpo
crafts.description: Household and small-workshop processing of staple traditional foods — flattened rice (chira), puffed rice (muri), date/palm molasses (gur), and preserved pickles (achar) — using traditional hand and hearth methods.
materials: Date palm or sugarcane sap (for gur)
Seasonal fruits/vegetables, mustard oil, and spices (for pickles)
tools: Large boiling pots (kadhai) and a claying/tapping knife for gur (rস collection from palm/date trees)
Sun-drying trays and storage jars for pickles
technique_steps: Chira: parboil and roast paddy, then flatten it by pounding in a dheki
Muri: roast soaked paddy rapidly in hot sand until it puffs

Gur: tap date-palm or sugarcane sap (traditionally at dawn from a fresh cut on the tree), then boil the sap for hours in a kadhai until it thickens into molasses, which is poured into molds to solidify
Pickles: sun-dry and marinate fruits/vegetables in oil, salt, and spices, then age in sealed jars for weeks to develop flavor
crafts.time_required: Chira/muri: a day per batch; gur: a full night-to-morning sap collection plus hours of boiling per batch during the winter tapping season; pickles: weeks of aging after initial preparation
crafts.skill_transmission: Widespread household and village-level seasonal knowledge, passed within families
regions: Gur (date-palm molasses): Jashore (a registered GI product — date molasses)
Chira/Muri: produced in rice-growing districts nationwide, notably Naogaon and Bogura
crafts.endangerment_level: Stable — deeply embedded in daily and festival food culture nationwide
crafts.notes: Jashore date molasses is a registered GI product.
